label: Institutional food production and distribution
interpretation: Successive supra-household food-production and distribution spaces show that durable public institutions developed outside the southern Uruk core.
limits: The 95.4% radiocarbon span bounds several phases; it is not the duration of one building or proof of a state.

label: Urbanization and emergent state formation
interpretation: Selz treats this as the main period of Uruk urbanization and state formation.
limits: The same synthesis says the sources do not unequivocally demonstrate monocratic governance. This is an interpretive period, not a recovered constitutional date.

label: Cylinder seals in use
interpretation: Cylinder seals and sealed clay devices expanded a pre-literate administrative repertoire before proto-cuneiform.
limits: Mid-fourth millennium is a broad dating phrase; sealing did not have one function or originate at one site.

label: Several-hundred-hectare city with monumental core
interpretation: Uruk had grown from a modest village to several hundred hectares and contained numerous monumental structures, extensive record-keeping, and redistribution.
limits: Surface footprint, monumentality, and institutional control are related evidence—not interchangeable definitions of a state.

label: Proto-cuneiform tablets
interpretation: The surviving script makes administrative classification and accounting directly visible.
limits: Many signs remain contested; first attestation is not necessarily the date of invention.

label: Uruk footprint
interpretation: Published approximate occupied area at the close of the fourth millennium.
limits: Edges may include or omit lower-density occupation; footprint is not population.

label: Uruk footprint
interpretation: Published approximate occupied area in the early third millennium.
limits: The source notes that many southern city-size estimates depend on older survey or imagery and on how edges are defined.

label: Northern urban hub
interpretation: Tell Brak reached an estimated 55 hectares before its later expansion.
limits: LC phases are broad; site footprint can contain discontinuous or low-density areas.

label: Expanded northern hub
interpretation: Published survey synthesis gives a later footprint of about 130 hectares.
limits: The date range is phase-level and the occupied area was not necessarily uniform through the whole interval.

label: Northern center
interpretation: A further large northern settlement shows that early urban trajectories were plural.
limits: The broad Late Chalcolithic label prevents annual comparison with Uruk.

label: Sparse, discontinuous settlement
interpretation: A very large but low-density and short-lived scatter preceded Uruk's 250-hectare city.
limits: The occupation was sparse, discontinuous, and possibly seasonal; total footprint alone does not make it comparable to a densely occupied city.
